concept: Worn brick and neon corner bar: an aged-copper primary (old tap lines and downtown brick) over smoky parchment with deep charcoal-brown ink, a blackened-steel secondary like night-window glass, and a neon-aqua accent lifted straight from a beer sign in the window. Warm and unpretentious by day, sign-glow by night — deliberately distinct from the fleet's golden-amber taproom (noon-whistle), brick-red grille (fattys), bottle-green taverns (pub-west, lord-stanleys), and the blue/red sports bar on the same street (mvps).
contrastNotes: All required ratios verified computationally (WCAG relative luminance). ink #251B12 on bg #F5EEE4 = 14.65:1, on surface #FDF9F2 = 16.08:1, on surface-alt #EBDFCC = 12.83:1 (all >=7). ink-soft #5C4A38 on bg = 7.32:1, on surface = 8.03:1, on surface-alt = 6.41:1 (all >=4.5). White on primary #8F4A1E = 6.63:1 (>=4.5); white on primary-dark #6F3714 = 9.41:1; white on secondary #2F3B44 = 11.48:1. Neon-aqua accent #58D2BF vs #222 = 8.63:1 and vs #000 = 11.39:1 (>=4.5 — safe rendered solid over dark photos on this edge:hard site). primary on bg = 5.76:1 (>=3). Accent is a light neon tone: pair it with dark ink for text-on-accent (ink on accent 9.15:1), never white.
